About Greenfields School
Schools
Welcome to Greenfields School, a vibrant educational haven where individuality thrives and education is for life!
We offer your child a unique independent education experience whether as a day or boarding student. They are nurtured, given learning tools to win in their studies and lessons in morals so as to reach their full potential in life and be happy. As a parent, we offer you the comfort of knowing that your child is in a safe, caring holistic learning environment that will encourage your child every step of the way towards a great future.
Greenfields is consistently recognised as one of the best boarding schools in Britain by our students, parents, alumni, education agents, international schools and our dedicated staff. Our schools is also a member of the Independent Schools Association.
We believe in nurturing the whole child and fostering a love of learning that extends far beyond the classroom.
At Greenfields, we are proud to present a unique and comprehensive private education experience. Our curriculum is designed to foster diversity and enrichment, guiding students through an exceptional educational voyage that sets the foundation for lifelong learning and success.
“[The School] actively promote the wellbeing of pupils by ensuring they are supported to individually achieve their full potential.” – Independent School Inspectorate (ISI) 2024
Preschool & Reception
Infants & Juniors
Seniors
Sixth Form

Education for Life
The School motto at Greenfields is “Education for Life”. What exactly does that mean? At Greenfields, we teach students how to be students. Our method enables an individual to study in such a way that they can understand and apply the data they are studying. Furthermore, they can utilise this method to their benefit throughout the rest of their life.
This method, known as “Study Technology”, makes study itself a pleasurable and worthwhile experience. It is a fantastic experience of acquiring knowledge, understanding, and ways of doing things that sets one up for life.
“As long as children and young men and women find pleasure in study, they will continue studying throughout life – and upon that depends their happiness.” – Hubbard
In line with this vision, Greenfields aims to make learning an engaging and fulfilling journey that inspires a lifelong pursuit of knowledge and growth. Additionally, Greenfields provides an education that goes beyond academics.
Here our approach prepares students not only for jobs but also for true maturity. We focus on more than academic knowledge. We also like to nurture a student’s practical life skills, emotional intelligence, and social abilities. Beyond studies, students learn how to be respectful, effective communicators, ready to engage harmoniously with the world around them.
Our mission is to nurture curious, capable, and compassionate individuals who leave Greenfields with the confidence and skills to lead meaningful lives. Here, education is not just preparation for a job; it’s preparation for life.
How Our Alumni Used Their Education For Life:
Omayma Ramzy
After Greenfields, Omayma gained a degree in fine art at the City and Guilds of London Art School. Omayma is now living in LA where she runs her own company called Omayma Inc., providing make-up, clothing and styling services to the stars. She has also worked on music videos and numerous TV commercials including for Ford and Samsung.
Ali Helnwein
Ali is an Emmy-winning composer and has orchestrated Grammy-winning projects.
In 2006 he founded the Traction Avenue Chamber Orchestra, which he has been successfully conducting since.
Becky Danese ( nee Hardy )
Becky is a writer and photographer, managing Grays of Westminster, an exclusive award-winning professional Nikon-only dealership in London, and their successful YouTube channel.
Assaff Rawner
Mark Roberts Motion Control is a revolutionary special effects company for the film industry used in most major films such as ‘the Matrix’, ‘Avatar’, ‘Harry Potter’ etc. Winners of a technical Oscar at the Academy Awards Hollywood 1999.

Personal Development
Personal Development
At Greenfields, we believe that the school should greatly help each child become a valuable, responsible member of society. Personal growth is a vital part of our formative years and we want to do everything we can to help prepare students for adulthood. The school and the parents are encouraged to work together to ensure that the individual child is not only academically achieving but also succeeding socially and emotionally.
Nursery & Reception
Joining school is a milestone for almost every child and is where social and academic education comes together in the classroom to assist a child to develop into a socially mature individual with skills for life. Children can enrol in the nursery from the age of 3 years, and have other children with them. Here they learn communication with others, share, play together and begin to learn how to resolve differences between themselves.
Their physical development is also addressed in, for instance, outdoor and indoor activities, washing hands, healthy eating, using small tools for hand-eye coordination, and dressing. They also take their first steps in literacy by learning phonics; mathematics by understanding numbers and quantity, and understanding the wider world through visits and visitors. They begin to develop self-expression in the arts.
The educational process continues in the reception class with a little more emphasis on the three “R’s”. These are reading, writing, and arithmetic, in preparation for their entry into school in Year 1.
Play is an important experience for children at this stage of their development. Together with active learning, creativity, and the ability to think, positively and critically. Teachers and assistants are aware of the three barriers to study when they teach and encourage children to understand that sometimes they may not understand and should say so. This is an important part of the development of a child’s learning in the classroom and in life. It is the foundation for the learning and use of the Study Technology, which in time will create an independent student with a skill for life.
Infants & Juniors
At Greenfields Infant and Junior School, we provide access to a high-quality education with a broad and balanced curriculum. It meets National Curriculum standards, prioritises personal growth and also provides excellent pastoral care that prepares students for the challenges and expectations of the modern world.
We achieve this by ensuring our students strive for excellent academic achievement, meet challenges and develop a love of learning. The vibrant curriculum and the application of the Study Technology (which teaches children how to learn and apply) support our children in becoming ready for Senior School and life.
Additionally, in the Infants and Juniors, we seek to support the personal development of all students by providing each with respect for British values and the development of positive personality traits which are integral to our ethos. Regular whole school assemblies, learning buddies, and The Way to Happiness lessons are a vital part of the curriculum. Hands-on activities, workshops, and visits from guests at the end of terms are an incentive for our students to try their hardest and develop a moral compass.
Through the Way to Happiness lessons, the children are encouraged to be proud of their own identity and respectful and tolerant of those around them. Every child is supported in becoming the best they can be, cherishing their relationships, being industrious, and learning how to care for themselves and their environment.
We are committed to creating a happy and active environment where all members of the school and the wider community are respected and valued. We support and encourage each other to be inspired to learn. We seek to equip all our pupils with the right tools to become independent learners in the future.
Senior School
House Teams
The Senior Students are allocated a house team when they enrol at Greenfields. The three houses are Romans, Trojans and Spartans. During the school year, the students are awarded points for various activities such as sporting matches, academic achievements, volunteering, assisting a teacher and more. The students have to work as a team and at the end of the school year, the winning team is awarded the house cup and a reward for their hard work. This encourages a sense of community and teamwork.
Careers
PVBA (Personal Values, Beliefs and Attitudes)
In Senior School, there is a lesson every week which covers a range of topics from different religions, world events, politics, drug education, sex education, human rights, and more. This is a great opportunity for the students to expand their knowledge of the world and to engage in conversations about those things that might otherwise not be discussed freely. It is during this time that the students also learn about the principles in The Way to Happiness, which is a non-religious moral code, designed for people to read and use to live happily with others.
Student Consultant
In the Senior School, the Student Consultant deals sensitively and expertly with student behavioural issues and oversees the moral, social and cultural development of the students. She is on hand to assist and support the students with any non-academic issues that they may have. To find out more about how our Student Consultant can help with personal growth, click the button below.

Tours and Open Days
Tours and Open Days
Tours and open days are a great way to find out more about Greenfields School. Book your visit and come to see our wonderful learning environment for yourself. More information on tours and open days can be found below:
Tours
You are welcome to book a meeting and tour with our Admissions Manager at any time to tour the Senior School, Primary School or Preschool. During the tour you will see all aspects of the school, meet students and staff, and discover what makes Greenfields unique. Where possible, the Executive Head likes to meet the student and parents and answer any further questions.
Tours are from Monday to Friday in term time and appointment times are: 9:30 am and 1:30 pm.
Contact the Admission Manager here to book your tour.

Dance & Music Lessons
Dance & Music Lessons
Dance
At Greenfields, dance pervades the school. Your child can join any number of dance classes that they wish, from the age of 3 years old to 18 years old.Through caring, structured classes the dance teacher seeks to enhance the development of the students throughout their entire educational experience. Our dance teacher has worked with the school for over 20 years and is highly skilled, qualified, talented, and passionate about providing the best dance education for your child.The aim is for children to have fun, enjoy dancing, express themselves creatively and develop their love for dance and theatre.Classes on offer: Ballet, Jazz, Modern, Tap, Contemporary, Hip Hop and Tumbling.
Children have the opportunity to advance through the ISTD grades and vocational graded examinations. They also perform annually in either choreographic shows or dance productions and compete in festivals.Children who choose to progress into vocational dance and musical theatre colleges are supported and encouraged and many have gone on to have successful careers in these fields.
Music
Children attend one to two music/singing lessons per week depending on age, where they begin to develop their understanding of music and singing. Playing a musical instrument or singing is actively encouraged at Greenfields.
Private music lessons can be arranged via our Ms Miri.

Headmasters Welcome
Headteacher
Hello – Welcome Greenfields Independent Day and Boarding School, a member of the Independent Schools Association, set on the edge of the Royal Ashdown Forest in twenty-nine acres of our own woodland.
Visitors to the school frequently notice that there’s something special about Greenfields. The school’s ethos underpins everything we do, and creates a creates a unique atmosphere of industriousness and camaraderie. This is something the school has been known for since its inception in the 1980s.
At Greenfields, we give students the essential knowledge and skills for living, in particular the ability and confidence to study, understand and apply any subject whatsoever. We achieve this by using the technology of study, as discovered and delineated by philosopher and educator Mr. L. Ron Hubbard, so that they can successfully follow whatever path they choose in life.
We are one of only a select number of schools to offer a continuity of education from preschool to university entrance. Students of all faiths, cultures and nationalities, aged from 2 to 18 receive an all-round education for life, and achieve excellent academic results. Boys and girls can join Greenfields at any age and at any time of year and we are open to students from all over the world and from all cultural, ethnic and religious backgrounds.
We are a family-sized school of under 250 students offering unique benefits, including a friendly, caring and safe environment with zero tolerance of drugs or bullying. We offer a great experience in our boarding area, with a real family atmosphere and attention to detail and care for every student.
We have a technology of study which ensures that children really understand and can therefore use the information they learn. At Greenfields, students are given the tools that allow them to learn and to feel really passionate about their interests and chosen fields. This allows them to prepare for work or university with the confidence that they will excel.
As a former Greenfields student, I personally know the value of a Greenfields education and Study Technology, and the success that its application brings. I graduated from the school in 1989, and went on to University to gain a degree in the Arts, and after that a primary teaching qualification.
I established myself a reputation as a top-class classroom practitioner, and moved into school leadership rapidly after that as Head of Maths in a Middle School (9-13 yrs). My experience leading maths led to a consultancy post for Sandwell LA, where I supported teachers in over 50 schools, and delivered national training programmes across the region.
I became Head Teacher of a school in Crawley in 2015. At that time, the school had the lowest results of all the Primary Schools in the town. I led the school for eight years, achieving an Ofsted ‘good’ rating in 2018. Under my leadership the school went from strength to strength with results in 2022 significantly exceeding the average score of all Primary Schools across the country.
Throughout my career, I have applied Study Technology in challenging circumstances to help children from greatly diverse backgrounds. In January 2024 I joined Greenfields School as the new Head Teacher. Greenfields School gives every student the broad and balanced education they need to succeed in their future learning and their adult life, and I’m delighted to be part of that story.
Andrew Hodgson
Headteacher, Greenfields School

Seniors
Seniors
Lower Senior
The Lower Seniors consist of Years 7, 8 and 9. In these first three years of Senior School, we aim to give every student a rounded education in a wide range of subjects and to open their eyes to the possibilities that lie ahead of them in the world at large.
As in the Infant and Junior School, education is based upon Greenfields’s curriculum, the National Curriculum and that of Cambridge. We assess each student regularly to determine their progress and to ensure that they are succeeding in all subjects. Tailor-made programmes can be made to suit each student. If a student is advancing quickly, then they can be challenged with more advanced work and if they need extra support, then they can receive the assistance that they need to resolve any problems and move forward.
We continue the process of teaching students how to learn from the Junior School into Lower Seniors with Study Technology with additional courses. Students then have more tools to overcome barriers that they may come across when studying and enable them to fully understand the information that they have learnt so that they can use it.
In Lower Seniors
All students have their class tutor who is responsible for the overall care, education, and parent liaison. Students register with their class tutor every morning and afternoon. Here the students have a chance to discuss anything with their tutor that they have their attention on. Subjects taught include Maths, English Language, English Literature, Physics, ICT (Computers), Chemistry, Biology, History, Geography, Art, Drama, Music, Sport, and Spanish. The Lower Seniors aim to give every individual enough of an overview of subjects for an informed choice to be made when it comes to deciding what will be studied for examinations in Years 10 and 11, and possible career choices.
It is in Year 9 that students select the subjects they wish to pursue in their GCSEs. Students who are in an English as a Second Language Programme currently can choose all subjects that have a * beside them, if they have graduated from the programme, they can choose any subject. These subjects include:
Other languages may also be taken as a GCSE exam if a student has an efficient standard of fluency in that language already and wishes to sit the examination. In addition to their chosen subjects, students continue to participate in Study Technology courses, further gaining more advanced study tools needed to achieve the confidence and abilities to progress in their area of study. This develops independence in students allowing them to be confident and motivated in their self-studies throughout their school curriculum and into their future.
Here at Greenfields we reccommend that the student take at least seven GCSE’s and definately no less than five. Maths and English are compulsory and whilst it is advised to take a Science, it is not mandatory.

Upper Senior
It is in Year 10 where students, having chosen their GCSE subjects are given individual class timetables. After registration students will go to the next lesson on their timetable.
The Upper senior years cover a GCSE (General Certificate of Secondary Education) qualification covering Years 10 and 11. These are some of the most important years as external examinations are taken through a range of UK exam boards. Students cover the content needed for that subject and complete mock examinations during Years 10 and 11 in preparation for what is expected in their final examinations. They also complete extensive revision in the months leading up to exams. Study Technology continues to be applied throughout the Senior years.
Schedule
The school day commences at 8:50 am in register with the class tutor and ends at 4:05 pm. This allows for all subjects to be covered within a range of lesson times as well as provides study room time for students to complete homework to further their studies and revise.

pageCache.pageTitle: Celebrating World Day for Cultural Diversity at Greenfields School - Greenfields School
pageCache.text:
Tamara Richardson
At Greenfields School, we pride ourselves on our diversity, with staff from over ten countries and students from even more. Celebrating World Day for Cultural Diversity was a meaningful way for us to bring our community together.
Many students came dressed in traditional clothing, showcasing the rich cultures represented at our school. Parents contributed by cooking dishes from their home countries for everyone to enjoy. It was a delightful culinary journey, giving students the chance to taste flavours from around the world.
In addition to the delicious food, students shared stories about their home countries, answering questions and educating their classmates about different cultures. The Primary School Drama Teacher brought a touch of Ireland to the celebration by teaching a lesson on Irish dancing, getting both students and teachers moving to the lively rhythms.
A highlight of the day was a special assembly where the Head Teacher and his band, featuring members from Scotland, England, Australia, and Hungary, performed songs from their home countries. The students loved the performance, which added a festive atmosphere to the celebration.
We extend a big thank you to all the parents who provided food, shared stories about their countries and contributed to making the day a success. Your involvement made this celebration truly special and memorable for everyone.

pageCache.pageTitle: End of Year Art Exhibits - Greenfields School
pageCache.text:
Tamara Richardson
Individual creativity is an essential part of education, providing a crucial platform to nurture the creativity, passion, and individuality of each student. The Art Department plays a pivotal role in this endeavour, encouraging students to be curious, courageous, and original within the realm of visual arts. Through a structured yet flexible curriculum, we empower our students to develop their ability to question, generate ideas and problem-solve, skills that are invaluable both within and beyond the classroom.
Fostering Curiosity and Courage
From the very beginning of their educational journey, our students are immersed in an environment that celebrates curiosity and innovation. The Art Department’s curriculum is designed to challenge students to think outside the box and explore new perspectives. By engaging with a wide range of media and disciplines, students are encouraged to experiment and take risks in their artistic endeavours. This approach not only enhances their technical skills but also builds their confidence in expressing their unique viewpoints.
Embracing Diverse Influences
A vital component of our art education is the exposure to the works of artists from diverse times and cultures. By studying these varied influences, students gain a broader understanding of the world and the many ways in which art reflects and shapes human experience. This cultural immersion informs and inspires their own emerging work, fostering a rich and diverse artistic community within our school.
The Importance of Drawing Practice
Drawing is a fundamental skill in the visual arts, and we ensure that it is a core part of our curriculum across all key stages. Regular drawing practice allows students to refine their techniques and develop a strong foundation in observational skills. By dedicating time to drawing throughout the school years, we help students build a solid base upon which they can expand their creative abilities.
Celebrating Student Achievements
The culmination of our students’ hard work and creativity is showcased at the end of each school year in our annual art exhibitions. These events provide an opportunity for students, parents and friends to celebrate the artistic achievements of our young artists. This year, the quality of the work was so impressive that we held two separate exhibits: one for Preschool and Primary School students and another for Senior School students. The pieces displayed were a testament to the exceptional talent and dedication of our students.
A Vibrant Artistic Community
Our art exhibitions are more than just a display of student work; they are a reflection of the vibrant and supportive artistic community we cultivate at our school. Each piece of art tells a story of exploration, growth, and personal expression. The exhibits allow us to honour the creativity and hard work of our students, while also inspiring others to pursue their artistic passions.
In conclusion, the Art Department is committed to nurturing the creativity and individuality of each student. Through a comprehensive and dynamic curriculum, we strive to develop not only skilled artists but also innovative thinkers and confident individuals. We are proud of the achievements of our students and look forward to continuing to support their creative journeys.

Independent Day and Boarding School
Sussex-based Independent Day and Boarding School
Places available for September 2024 – 2025 Admission – Book a private tour or come to our Open Afternoon on Friday, 14th June, at 1:30 pm. Call us to book your tour or confirm your attendance for the Open Afternoon.
Welcome to Greenfields Day and Boarding School
Greenfields is a small, independent day and boarding school offering both weekly and full-time boarding. As a non-denominational private school, we have students from all different backgrounds and faiths and they all get along great.
The school is set in the heart of the East Sussex countryside surrounded by forestry, fields and lakes and just five minutes away is the quaint village of Forest Row and we are twenty minutes from Gatwick Airport.
Why Greenfields School
Now Enrolling
Individual assessments & programmes
Find out our fees, get a prospectus, book a tour, or ask as a question.
Our Curriculum
Unlike many other schools, Greenfields has open admissions throughout the year. Due to our diverse ways of teaching, students are given complimentary entry assessments in Maths, English and all three Sciences. These assessment results, whether below average or above, are evaluated in great detail to place your child where he/she will succeed best. Any student who is displaying gaps in their learning from the previous years is given a personal ‘catch-up’ program to keep them on track. Likewise, any student who is above their year level will also be accommodated, keeping them feeling challenged.
We recognise that children have not always been taught to learn, which inhibits them from being able to comprehend fully, as well as think and act on the information. Additionally, we show students how to study with exceptional study tools, coupled with the Cambridge Curriculum framework in some subjects and National Curriculum, which results in a more focused student who is on track for a bright future!
We host both male and female students in boarding from the ages of 11 (Year 7) to -18 years. Students come from across the UK and internationally which creates a unique and exciting place to study and call home. Boarding students are cared for and looked after by our friendly boarding supervisors who ensure our students are performing academically well and feel comfortable in our family-style environment.
If you are looking for weekly boarding schools or full boarding, we can offer either 5 days a week for those wishing to go home on the weekends or 7 days a week for those students whose homes are further afield or who wish to stay and participate in the weekend excursions. Our fees are very affordable with generous discounts as the student progresses through the school.
Find out more or book a tour
Boarding Facilities
All meals are locally sourced and cooked on the premises. This consists of three healthy, delicious meals: breakfast, lunch and dinner, as well as snacks. Special diets (including Allergies, Vegetarian, Halal, Gluten Free etc.) are taken into account where this is needed. There is a boarding kitchen with healthy food and snacks available at all times. All boarders have the chance to go to the local supermarket once a week to purchase needed items or treats. There are also outings mid-week to the local leisure centre or shopping at the local supermarket.
Boarders also have access to the Boarders’ Lounge where they can relax with friends or alone. There are numerous activities and games for their entertainment, as well as secure internet access.
Activities
Activities are arranged in the evening and at weekends after the school day is complete. Weekend activities can include horse-riding and sailing in the Summer, shopping, go-carting, visiting famous landmarks of England or simply a fun day out! There is a tennis court, basketball court, football pitch and hockey pitch on site and students can join the local gym. We also have over 25 acres of land, so there is plenty of space in which to explore and exercise, keeping the students minds and bodies fit.
In the evenings, run by our boarding supervisors, there is a homework/study slot where students can keep up with their academics and complete any preparations needed for the next school day.
Affordable Fees and Generous Discounts
Greenfields aims to keep its fees comparatively low. There is a sibling discount and a generous longevity discount as a student moves up through the school, this allows a private education to be more easily accessible to your family. Fees are adjusted according to the entry year group and depending on requirements e.g. Boarding, EAL (English as an Additional Language), or Sixth Form. Grant your child the wonderful of experience of our independent day and boarding school at Greenfields.
Our admissions team will be happy to assist in explaining how this works clearly and concisely
Tours
At Greenfields we prefer the personal approach with tours, giving you more time to ask questions and get answers. Tours are conducted during the term so that you experience our school on a normal working day. They are Monday to Friday at 10.00 am, 1.00 pm and 2.30 pm. If you are unable to come for a tour, the Admissions Manager can arrange a video call with you.
Find our fees, get a prospectus, ask a question, or book a tour
To find out our fees for your child, book a tour, or if you have any questions at all regarding if your child can enter Greenfields at this time, please get in touch with the Admissions team below. They will be able to answer your questions and would be happy to help. You can also request a Prospectus hard copy and more detailed information about our independent day and boarding school.

Infants & Juniors
Infants & Juniors
Infants
The Infants consists of Year 1 and Year 2. It is in these classes that the children build on the firm foundations laid down in the Reception class. It is from Year 1 that formal education begins and it is based upon Greenfields’s curriculum, the National Curriculum and that of Cambridge. The curriculum is used in such a way as to best fit the individual students and their needs. This level of individual care continues through to Advanced Level Studies in the Sixth Form.
In these years, we are very careful in making sure that the children understand all the words that are being used and they are encouraged to ask what something means if they do not understand. Teachers avoid going on to another step before the children have understood the current one and they ensure that the children are given examples of the things that they are being taught.For more details on how we use this Study Technology throughout the School, please click here.
Children benefit from having more one-to-one attention in the Greenfields setting. Assessment is continuous so a child can be challenged and move ahead or be assisted to stay on target.It is in Infants that reading and writing really start to take off and the children move rapidly through a series of carefully graded books and other material designed to enhance and stretch their skills. They address spelling, vocabulary, grammar and punctuation, reading and writing, presentation, speaking, and listening. They are given many opportunities to write and take pride in presenting a neat piece of work. Maths is taught traditionally with emphasis on knowing and understanding basic arithmetic.
The Infants Science Curriculum is topic-based and involves many practical aspects, which are not only fun but educational.
Other subjects are introduced in these classes and incorporated into the timetable as topics of study.The children enjoy sports lessons twice a week, whether outside on the tennis courts, football pitch or inside in our gymnasium.Every step of the way, the focus is on adding value to your child’s educational experience.
Schedule
The school day begins at 9 am and finishes at 3 pm. There are extracurricular activities from 3 pm to 4 pm daily.
Extra-Curricular
The extracurricular activities are from 3 pm to 4 pm daily. There are also some activities during lunchtime. These activities change every half term and are charged as an additional cost.
Juniors
The Junior School consists of Years 3, 4, 5, and 6. The teachers are friendly, caring, and passionate about educating each child and helping them fulfill their true potential. As in the Infant School, education is based upon Greenfields’s curriculum, the National Curriculum, and that of Cambridge. The curriculum is used in such a way as to best fit the individual students and their needs. This level of individual care continues through to Advanced Level Studies in the Sixth Form.
Reading
In this age of television and computer games, Greenfields is aware of the importance of vocabulary building and reading. We have an excellent reading programme which starts in the Infants, continues throughout Juniors and into the Lower Seniors. Ever wider reading is constantly encouraged.
Writing
The children learn how to write stories, poems, instructions, letters, reports, etc. They study and analyse the writings of others to help stimulate their creative writing. Handwriting is taught with the aim of each student acquiring a neat, legible, cursive style through continuous practice in the Junior years, and students also complete a Grammar and Communication Course which provides a wonderful foundation for all later education.
Mathematics
The Maths curriculum is supplemented with an in-house maths scheme, which comprises individual booklets and a series of class games and activities for each year. The intention is to instil in children a lasting enjoyment of maths and problem-solving.
Science
This subject is taught in projects. The first steps are an introduction to simple concepts such as weather, the human body and simple machines. In the next class, children study more of the actual biological and physical environments such as plant life and sound. In the older Junior classes, the students begin simple experiments and observations related to everyday life and the world around them.
Sport
The children enjoy sports lessons twice a week, whether outside on the tennis courts, football pitch or inside in our gymnasium.
Additional Information
Additional subjects such as Geography, History, Art, and ICT all form part of the Year 3-6 timetables. In the Junior classes, Science, Math, Art, Sport, and ICT are sometimes taught by specialist teachers. During break times, the children get to make the most of the beautiful setting, as the playground is located in the Ashdown Forest. This year a brand new outdoor decking has been built in the forest. This provides an inspirational place for the children to learn, play and use their imagination.

The Margaret Hodkin Creative Arts Centre
The Schools founder, Margaret Hodkin’s first love was the creative arts. She started the famous Greenfields Theatre Company, which produces shows every year. In these shows all students in the school are involved–with scripting, directing, producing, acting, props and scenery, lighting, promotion and marketing, accounting etc. In the early days, Margaret personally supervised this activity for several years. Greenfields is an enduring legacy of Margaret, but we have also decided to honour her life with a new facility at Greenfields–the Margaret Hodkin Creative Arts Centre. Combining drama, dance, music and song in a purpose-built building named after Margaret will ensure that future generations will not only have a place to develop all of their creative talents but will also know the person who started it all.
We invite anyone who knew Margaret or who wants to support this exciting new project to make a donation. Our History
Our History
Greenfields School was founded on the 13th of July 1981 by educator Margaret Hodkin who, familiar with the benefits of Study Technology, wanted to establish a school that utilised this remarkable technology and encouraged a love of the arts and creativity in general. It started in a small vicarage in a village called Hammerwood, not far from its current location in Forest Row, to where it moved in 1983.
Beginning with just three classes, Infants, Juniors and Seniors, it has evolved over the years to become an outstanding school providing a real education for pupils ranging in age from 3 years to 18 years.
It has been a member of the Independent School’s Association for most of its history.
Word of its successful approach using Study Technology has been spreading; It is now expanding its facilities to meet the increased demand for its unique approach to learning.
The founder of Greenfields School, Margaret Hodkin (Neal), passed away on 1st May 2019.
In 1955 she was awarded an honours degree in English by Kings College, University of London and was offered the Inglis Studentship as the best student of her year; Margaret then taught and lectured in English at several schools and colleges.
In 1981, together with Mike Neal (who she later married), she purchased an old vicarage in Hammerwood, East Sussex and opened Greenfields School.
They started with 30 students; The numbers rose to 60 by the end of the first term and continued.
In 1982 she created the Greenfields Educational Trust registered charity, which took over the guardianship of the school when it moved to its present home in Forest Row in 1983.
Margaret was a pioneer of Mr Hubbard’s Study Technology in education.
Margaret’s vision was to use Study Technology in conjunction with a conventional United Kingdom academic curriculum to enable students to not only do well in examinations but also to apply, in life, what they had learnt.
They would have the tools to do anything they wanted with their lives.
And so it has proved, with students of her school going on to be leaders in many fields – including law, medicine, engineering, academics, business, entertainment and numerous others.
Margaret later became an inspector of schools for the Independent School’s Association but continued teaching and tutoring and preparing them for GCSE examinations right up to the end of her life.
But Margaret’s first love was the creative arts.
She started the famous Greenfields Theatre Company, which produces shows every year in which all students in the school are involved – with scripting, directing, producing, acting, props and scenery, lighting, promotion and marketing, accounting etc. In the early days, Margaret personally supervised this activity for some years.
The Greenfields Theatre Company continues to this day.
